title: Making, DIY and Drawing
subtitle: Foam models, custom keyboards, a 3D-printer rebuild, drawing
context: Models made for school projects, personal builds and drawing practice
summary: This page collects the hands-on work behind my projects: foam and 3D-printed models for an angle grinder, a car and a hair dryer, keyboards I designed and built, and an upgrade kit for an older 3D printer. It ends with drawing, colour and art-history exercises.

sections.heading: Angle grinder models
sections.body: For the electric angle grinder project, yellow foam was used for modeling iteration, and the final model was made with red high-density foam.

sections.heading: Car model
sections.body: For the car project, the base is handcrafted from high-density red foam, and the exterior is 3D printed.

sections.heading: Hair dryer model
sections.body: The entire model is handmade from high-density red foam.

sections.heading: Custom keyboards
sections.body: Because I am interested in the craftsmanship and structure of keyboards, I spent a lot of time researching them and then tried different processes, such as 3D printing and laser-cut acrylic, to make my own. I did all the design drawings and processing drawings myself.

sections.heading: Upgrading an older 3D printer
sections.body: I have a basic Ender 3. The idea of this project was to let Ender 3 enthusiasts upgrade the machine to a high-speed printer with a Core XY structure just by buying some new accessories and printing their own structural parts.

sections.heading: Drawing and colour
sections.body:
These include some of my earliest paintings and colour works, and some product hand-drawing exercises.

The art-history practice followed the course of art history: I researched and analysed the styles and painting methods of artists in different periods and imitated them. It is an exercise to learn art history and feel the development of painting.
